subject: maths
card: Read clocks to the minute, the 24-hour clock, how long things take, and units of time.
title: Telling the time
seo_title: Telling the time practice: clocks, 24-hour time and durations (KS2)
description: Learn to tell the time on an analogue clock, to the nearest minute, convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time, work out how long things take, and convert units of time. Free practice with clock pictures for ages 9 to 11.
intro: When does the film start? How long until lunch? Learn to read any clock, use the 24-hour clock, and work out how long things take.

units.title: O'clock, half past and quarter past and to
units.blurb: The two hands, and the four easiest times.

learn.p: The **short hand** shows the hour. The **long hand** shows the minutes. When the long hand points straight up at 12, it's something o'clock. This clock shows 3 o'clock.
When the long hand points down at 6, it has gone half way round: **half past**. The short hand is half way between two numbers. This is half past 3.
Long hand at 3: **quarter past** (15 minutes past). Long hand at 9: **quarter to** (15 minutes to the next hour). This clock shows quarter to 4. The short hand is nearly at 4.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand points at 12. Where is the short hand?
questions.explain: Long hand at 12 means o'clock. The short hand points at 7, so it's 7 o'clock.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: Long hand at 6 means half past. The short hand is between 9 and 10: which hour has just gone?
questions.explain: The short hand has gone past 9, so it's half past 9.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: Long hand at 3 means quarter past.
questions.explain: Long hand at 3: quarter past. The short hand is just past 2: quarter past 2.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: Long hand at 9 means quarter to. The short hand is nearly at which number?
questions.explain: Long hand at 9: quarter to. The short hand is nearly at 12, so it's quarter to 12.

questions.q: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
questions.hint: An hour is 60 minutes. Find a quarter of 60.

questions.q: At half past 4, where is the short hand?
questions.hint: The short hand moves slowly from one hour to the next.
questions.explain: After half an hour, the short hand has moved half of the way from 4 to 5.

units.title: Minutes past and minutes to
units.blurb: Read the clock to the nearest minute.

learn.p: Each number on the clock is 5 more minutes. Long hand on 1 = 5 minutes past, on 2 = 10 past, on 4 = 20 past, on 5 = 25 past. This clock shows 20 past 8.
Up to the 6 we say **past** the hour. After the 6 we count the minutes left **to** the next hour. Long hand on 8: 20 minutes to. This clock shows 20 to 6.
Between the numbers are small marks, one for each minute. Count on from the last number. Long hand 2 marks after the 4: 20 + 2 = 22 minutes past.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand is on 2. Count in fives: 5, 10.
questions.explain: Long hand on 2 is 10 minutes past. Short hand just past 6: 10 past 6.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand is on 5. Count in fives.
questions.explain: Long hand on 5: 25 minutes past. Short hand just past 1: 25 past 1.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand is on 10, after the 6. How many minutes are left until the next hour?
questions.explain: Long hand on 10 is 50 minutes past, which leaves 10 minutes to the next hour. The short hand is nearly at 11: 10 to 11.

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand is on 7: 35 minutes past. How many are left to 60?

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.hint: The long hand is 2 small marks past the 3. The 3 is 15 minutes.

questions.q: It is 20 to 8. How many minutes is it until 8 o'clock?
questions.hint: “20 to” tells you!

units.title: am, pm and the 24-hour clock
units.blurb: Bus times, TV guides and phone clocks.

learn.p: A day has 24 hours, but a clock face only shows 12. So we say **am** for times from midnight to midday (morning) and **pm** for times from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening).
Phones and timetables often count the hours from 0 to 23. Morning times look the same, with a 0 in front if needed: 7:30 am is 07:30. For pm times, add 12 to the hour: 3:15 pm is 15:15.
To go from the 24-hour clock to pm, take 12 away: 19:40 is 7:40 pm. Midday is 12:00 and midnight is 00:00.

questions.q: Write 4:30 pm in 24-hour time.
questions.hint: It's pm, so add 12 to the hour.

questions.q: Write 08:05 as a 12-hour time.
questions.hint: The hour is less than 12, so it's in the morning.

questions.q: Write 21:45 as a 12-hour time.
questions.hint: Take 12 away from the hour.

questions.q: Which time is in the afternoon?
questions.hint: Afternoon times are 12:00 or later on the 24-hour clock.
questions.explain: 14:20 is 2:20 pm. The others are all before midday.

questions.q: What is midnight on the 24-hour clock?
questions.hint: The day starts again at midnight.
questions.explain: Midnight is 00:00, the start of a new day. Midday is 12:00.

questions.q: A train leaves at quarter past 6 in the evening. How is that shown on the timetable?
questions.hint: Quarter past 6 is 6:15. Evening means pm.

units.title: How long does it take?
units.blurb: Work out start times, end times and durations.

learn.p: A film starts at 2:40 pm and ends at 4:15 pm. Count on: 2:40 to 3:00 is 20 minutes, 3:00 to 4:00 is 1 hour, 4:00 to 4:15 is 15 minutes. Altogether 1 hour 35 minutes.
Time doesn't work in hundreds! There are 60 minutes in an hour, so 1:50 + 20 minutes is 2:10, not 1:70.
With the 24-hour clock you can't mix up morning and afternoon. 09:30 to 13:00 is 3 hours 30 minutes.

questions.q: Swimming starts at 3:15 pm and ends at 4:00 pm. How many minutes is that?
questions.hint: From 3:15 to 4:00, count on to the hour.

questions.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:40 am and needs 35 minutes. When is it ready?
questions.hint: 20 minutes takes you to 12:00. How many minutes are left?

questions.q: A film starts at 6:50 pm and lasts 1 hour 25 minutes. When does it end?
questions.hint: Add the hour first, then the minutes.
questions.explain: 6:50 + 1 hour = 7:50. Then 10 minutes to 8:00 and 15 more: 8:15 pm.

questions.q: A train leaves at 09:35 and arrives at 11:10. How long is the journey?
questions.explain: 25 minutes to 10:00, then 1 hour 10 minutes to 11:10. 25 + 10 = 35 minutes, plus 1 hour: 1 hour 35 minutes.

questions.q: School ends at 3:20 pm. Your walk home takes 25 minutes. When do you get home?
questions.hint: Add 25 minutes to 20 minutes past 3.

questions.q: A football match kicks off at 15:00 and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes with the break. When does it finish?
questions.hint: Add 1 hour, then 50 minutes.

learn.p: 60 seconds = 1 minute. 60 minutes = 1 hour. 24 hours = 1 day. 7 days = 1 week. 12 months = 1 year.
April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days, or 29 in a **leap year**. All the others have 31 days.
A year has 365 days, or 366 in a leap year. A leap year usually comes every 4 years (2024 and 2028 are leap years).

questions.q: How many minutes are in 3 hours?
questions.hint: 1 hour = 60 minutes.

questions.q: How many seconds are in 2 minutes?
questions.hint: 1 minute = 60 seconds.

questions.q: How many days are in 5 weeks?
questions.hint: 1 week = 7 days.

questions.q: How many hours are in 2 days?
questions.hint: 1 day = 24 hours.

questions.q: Which month has 30 days?
questions.hint: April, June, September and November.
questions.explain: June has 30 days. July, August and December have 31.

questions.q: How long is 90 minutes?
questions.hint: Take away 60 minutes to make 1 hour.

questions.q: How many days are in a leap year?
questions.hint: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day, in February.
